questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG shows a regular rhythm with a consistent 1:1 P-to-QRS relationship and normal waveform morphology at a notably slow rate. What is the underlying rhythm?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation with slow ventricular response

explanation.summary: A slow rate with an upright P wave preceding every QRS in a 1:1 fashion and normal PR interval indicates the impulse still originates in the SA node, defining sinus bradycardia rather than a junctional, blocked, or ectopic rhythm.
explanation.whyCorrect: A slow rate with an upright P wave preceding every QRS in a 1:1 fashion and normal PR interval indicates the impulse still originates in the SA node, defining sinus bradycardia rather than a junctional, blocked, or ectopic rhythm.

questions.stem: This ECG illustration counts the small boxes between two consecutive R waves to calculate heart rate. What calculation does this method use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Multiply the number of small boxes by 0.04 seconds

choices.label: B
choices.text: Divide 300 by the number of large boxes between R waves

choices.label: C
choices.text: Count QRS complexes in a 6-second strip and multiply by 10

choices.label: D
choices.text: Divide 60 by the R-R interval measured in large boxes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Divide 1500 by the number of small boxes between R waves

explanation.summary: The precise R-R small-box method divides 1500 (small boxes per minute at 25 mm/s) by the number of small boxes between consecutive R waves to yield beats per minute.
explanation.whyCorrect: The precise R-R small-box method divides 1500 (small boxes per minute at 25 mm/s) by the number of small boxes between consecutive R waves to yield beats per minute.

questions.stem: This rhythm strip shows a regular narrow-complex rhythm at roughly 130 bpm with a normal upright P wave preceding every QRS. What rhythm is this?

explanation.summary: A fast but regular rhythm with a normal P wave before each QRS and a constant PR interval indicates the SA node is simply firing faster, defining sinus tachycardia rather than a reentrant or ectopic tachyarrhythmia.
explanation.whyCorrect: A fast but regular rhythm with a normal P wave before each QRS and a constant PR interval indicates the SA node is simply firing faster, defining sinus tachycardia rather than a reentrant or ectopic tachyarrhythmia.
